title: Prefill Negotiator: latency-fairness heuristic using kernel hints and attention pressure
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our existing prefill/decode arbitration operates on coarse tenant weights and deadline buckets which causes two recurring issues in production: (1) tenants with bursty short prompts suffer headroom starvation when larger long-context requests dominate kernel selection, and (2) kernel selection decisions (e.g., int8 vs fp16 fusion kernels) are made without using attention density signals, causing suboptimal tail latency for attention-heavy workloads.

Goal: Implement a "Prefill Negotiator" stage in the runtime scheduler that uses lightweight kernel-hinting signals plus an attention-pressure estimator to split prefill/decode phases more adaptively. The negotiator should: (a) bias short-latency requests toward low-latency kernels and micro-slices when possible, (b) preserve throughput for long streaming/decoding flows by opportunistic merging, and (c) maintain proportional fairness across tenants (soft guarantees) subject to SLOs.

Design summary:
- Kernel hints: augment request metadata with two cheap signals produced by the model-metadata service: preferred_kernel_profile (e.g., fused_int8_v2, fp16_fused_attention, sparse-attn-probe) and attention_expectation (LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH). Hints are conservative defaults and are not binding.
- Attention-pressure estimator: a rolling-statistic computed from token geometry and recent KV cache growth (attn_pressure metric) that predicts incremental attention compute cost per token. Implemented as an O(1) estimator per request to avoid scheduling CPU bottlenecks.
- Negotiator policy: a three-way decision tree per scheduling opportunity: 1) Fast-path: if request length <= short_threshold AND preferred_kernel_profile suggests a low-latency kernel AND attn_pressure==LOW => assign micro-slice with low-latency kernel eviction hint. 2) Merge-path: if request is long OR attn_pressure==HIGH => attempt to merge with compatible long-batch kernel lane (throughput-optimized). 3) Balance-path: otherwise use proportional fairness token-credit allocator with soft latency boost if SLA_violation_risk is set.
- Phase splitting: implement microphase split points at token boundaries where attention_pressure crosses thresholds; merges are allowed when contiguous microphases share kernel compatibility.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs observability: adding kernel hints increases telemetry dimensionality but avoids blind kernel demotions; we limit hint cardinality to 4 profiles to keep dashboarding usable.
- Predictive correctness: attention_expectation is noisy; we treat it as prior and rely on runtime attn_pressure correction to avoid harmful demotions.
- Fairness vs SLOs: we prioritize preventing high-severity SLO breaches over strict proportional fairness (i.e., short tenant soft-boosts can temporarily exceed share). This is documented and surfaced in Console as "negotiator boost" events.

Instrumentation & success metrics:
- Primary metrics: 95th token latency for short requests (-10% target), mean throughput for long requests (within -2% of baseline), proportion of negotiator boosts per tenant (<3% of requests per tenant per hour).
- Safety gates: no increase in error-rate or kernel OOMs; quantile-tracked kernel demotions must have <0.1% regression.

Implementation plan:
1) Add kernel hint fields to internal model-metadata API and SDK. (engine infra change)
2) Implement attn_pressure estimator in runtime hot path (C++); micro-bench and unit tests.
3) Implement negotiator decision tree as pluggable policy module with feature flags.
4) A/B experiment in canary region (10% traffic) with extended tracing and cost accounting.
5) Rollout with guardrail toggles for tenant-group overrides.

Rollout & fallback: Start in canary for host-api customers with opt-in flag. If tail latency increases for any tenant group >5% within 30m, auto-fallback to legacy arbitration. Also expose per-tenant toggle in Dedicated deploy config.

Open questions:
- Short_threshold tuning: initial value 32 tokens; needs calibration per model family.
- Kernel compatibility matrix: need input from runtime/kernel team to list safe merges (especially for quantized kernels).
- Whether to persist attn_pressure across retries / retries with different kernels.

Related links: see comments for design doc, dashboard, and PRs.
